chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Which time is most beloved to you for departing from Jam'?' He said: 'A little before the sun rises, that is the most beloved of the times to me.' I said: 'And if we remain until the sun rises?' He said: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.أُفِيض: To depart or move forward (from a place)
key_terms.جَمْع: Muzdalifa, the sacred site where pilgrims spend the night after standing at Arafat

ai.seo_question: What is the best time to leave Muzdalifa during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the preferred time (mustahabb) for departing Muzdalifa before sunrise, reflecting the Imam’s preference for completing the ritual while the night still lingers. However, it clarifies that delaying until after sunrise does not invalidate the rite, offering flexibility for pilgrims who may be delayed. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing strict adherence to prophetic tradition with practical ease in Hajj rituals.
